synopsis: The simulation specialist’s three core objections are an unvalidated model, simulator architecture frozen against assumed hardware, and metrics chosen for convenience after results are known; the hostile review ranks the simulator’s unearned right to replace physical evidence as its strongest objection [f14949, f14525]. Credibility requires a defined validity envelope and evidence beyond internal consistency, because shared simplifying assumptions across the virtual sensor, collision logic and test oracle can produce consistent but misleading results [f10593, f14952, f10606]. The toolchain is built against assumed hardware until mid-2027, while changes to sensors, mounting, controller timing or the brake controller in 2027 can invalidate it without impact analysis; the specialist therefore recommends resolving supplier dependencies before architecture freeze and reserving physical re-correlation tests [f14954, f14955, f14956]. Metrics and thresholds should be declared prospectively, absence of agreed correlation metrics by early 2027 is a warning sign, and physical confirmatory tests should be selected by the assessor or risk analysis rather than convenience [f14957, f14959, f14958]. Before committing to the plan, the specialist recommends a credibility-framework pilot and an evidence package covering independent held-out physical validation, uncertainty and sensitivity analysis, configuration control, revalidation rules and explicitly unsupported claims [f10602, f14961]. The cited European automated-vehicle credibility requirements are explicitly on-road, while the planning guidance calls for recording dissenting technical opinions rather than leaving objections undocumented [f14951, f10234].

relations.note: Both identify an uncalibrated, unvalidated simulator lacking a defined validity envelope.
Both describe misleading consistency caused by shared simplifying assumptions.
Both describe the same seven hostile-review perspectives.
The glossary specifies strongest objection; the synthesis places it among the top three.
Explains the unvalidated-model objection as a measurement-instrument credibility problem.
Dates the assumed-hardware problem to mid-2027 and ties credibility to validated configuration.
Specifies prospective metrics and thresholds as protection against retrospective metric selection.
Common-mode errors explain why virtual evidence has not earned substitution rights.
Real-application validation addresses the insufficiency of internally consistent virtual results.
The on-road credibility requirements provide a cited rationale for adopting a credibility framework.
Details the evidence package needed to address simulator credibility objections.
Places proof against model-uncertainty dominance within a broader reviewer evidence package.
Identifies specific 2027 hardware changes that threaten configuration-specific simulator credibility.
Supplier resolution, early sensor freeze and re-correlation respond to hardware-change invalidation risk.
Missing correlation metrics by early 2027 signals failure to establish prospective acceptance measures.
Specifies missing residuals, uncertainty and validity approval behind misleading scenario-count claims.
Substitution savings require the simulator first earning the right to replace physical evidence.
Recording dissent preserves the technical objections elicited through the seven-perspective hostile review.
